records.issue_text: [High/security] app/models/post.rb:131 (with topic_embed.rb / poll_feed.rb / best.html.erb:19) — the new `raw_html` cook method stores external HTML as `cooked` with zero sanitization (PollFeed passes RSS `i.content` through completely unfiltered; the readability path filters tag/attribute names but not URL schemes, so `javascript:` hrefs survive), and best.html.erb renders it with `raw post.cooked` — a compromised/malicious feed or article yields stored XSS on both the embedding site and the forum
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: post.rb's cook returns raw for raw_html; TopicEmbed.import passes external contents directly (PollFeed uses CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) with no sanitization; the readability path only limits tags/attributes, not URL schemes); best.html.erb renders `raw post.cooked`. Malicious RSS/article content thus becomes stored XSS on the embed page and forum. Verified directly from the diff.

records.issue_text: [High/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — the feed-supplied `url` is interpolated unescaped into `<a href='#{url}'>` in the "imported from" footer; the only validation is the `^https?://` prefix check, so a link containing a single quote breaks out of the attribute and injects arbitrary HTML/JS into the post
records.rationale: In topic_embed.rb the only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\/\//`, and the footer interpolates `\"#{url}\"` unescaped. A URL with a single quote (e.g. `http://evil.com/' onmouseover=...`) breaks out of the attribute; since cook_method is raw_html (cooked == raw), the injected HTML is rendered verbatim in the post. Plausible injection mechanism is fully verifiable from the diff, though severity depends on attacker controlling feed URLs — with RSS polling enabled, that is realistic.

records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column :posts, :cook_method, default: 1, null: false` forces a full table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PG < 11, which can lock the posts table for a long time on large production forums
records.rationale: The diff does add `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` in db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb. On the PostgreSQL versions of that era (<11), adding a column with a non-null default forces a full table rewrite while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, and posts is the largest table in a Discourse forum. This is a factual, specific operational concern about a migration in this diff — not a correctness bug and not a style nit — relevant to shipping/rolling out this change on large production sites. The migration also lacks `disable_ddl_transaction!`
